messages:
james: Heads up — since ~04:12UTC we've seen a small spike of Xid 13 and Xid 31 on A10 nodes in ap-southeast1. Pattern looks different from the usual nightly embedder surge.

marta: which racks/rows are affected? any ECC counters rising?

james: r03 and r07 primarily. ECC counters normal-ish; not huge. logs show repeated `Xid 13` followed by soft-drv resets. sample log: `gpu0: Xid 13, PID 4821, decode kernel fault`

kai: could be small-batch low-latency tenants — I remember a week ago we saw Xid13 on tiny token bursts when NV drivers hit a scheduling corner. have we correlated to op types?

james: quick corelation: 85% of traces are small text-gen traffic (<=16 tokens) routed to A10 pool. embedding jobs not implicated.

oncall-matt: ops-bot ran a quick health check, posting results: 
```
ops-bot: gpu_health_check --rack r03,r07 --summary
r03: 2 nodes with >=5 Xid events in 1h, soft reset count 2
r07: 3 nodes with sporadic Xid13, nvlink flaps small
thermal: no sustained high temps
network: transient 95th pct p95 spikes on top-of-rack NIC 2
```

marta: interesting — NIC spikes + small-batch churn could be triggering stalls that expose driver timing bugs. any recent kernel/driver changes in that region?

kai: last driver roll was 10 days ago for ap-southeast1 (v520.61 -> v520.70). change log mentioned PCIe resync fixes. could be regression.

james: I pulled kube and runtime traces: `kubectl describe pod` shows a flurry of `OOM`? no, rather `device lost` messages right before resets. Tenant queue lengths hit 0.2ms bursts.

marta: action proposal: (1) isolate one suspect node, run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTILIZATION` and keep traffic reproducing, (2) move small-batch latency tenants off A10 pool to H100 burst pool for 6 hours, (3) mark nodes with >=5 Xid events for softdrain + hardware inspection.

kai: +1 to isolating. also suggest enabling driver verbose logs on those nodes (`NVREG_LOG_VERBOSITY=3`) and collect per-request optype traces so we can filter by token shape.

james: I'll schedule the tenant shift as a low-risk migration starting 05:00UTC. tagging nodes: r03-n4, r07-n2, r07-n5. planning softdrain commands: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then attach to maint queue.

oncall-matt: I've added a tally in the incident board: https://rwd/infracases/3890012345 — will post driver logs there.

marta: long-term: if this repeats, consider policy to route tiny token shapes to nodes with newer driver/firmware or to H100 as default. cost tradeoff but reduces noisy noisy neighbor Xid surface.

kai: can we run a quick repro with a synthetic small-batch gen workload on a quarantined node to validate? I can spin up a reproducer container that sends 8-token requests at 600rps for 10m.

james: please run it after I cordon r03-n4 (ETA 10m). tag me when logs are ready.

marta: noted — tagging @hardware-team for board inspection if softdrain shows retries. Also pinging @platform on whether the routing shim can be adjusted to avoid A10 for <32 token requests temporarily.

kai: one more note — Xid31 showed up intermittently too, sometimes followed by nvlink flaps in ops-bot's net logs. that points to PCIe or link-level resyncs, not pure compute kernel faults. collecting `dmesg` and `lspci -vvv` next.

james: summary of next steps: cordon/softdrain r03-n4, run reproducer, collect `nvidia-smi -q`, `dmesg`, driver verbose logs; migrate tiny-token tenants off A10 for 6h; open support ticket with vendor if hardware looks flaky. i'll update thread when we have repro. :thumbsup:
